original_question: For the same generic 3-dimensional single-input time-optimal problem q˙ = f(q) + u g(q), |u| <= 1, define sw(q) to be the least integer k such that every time-optimal trajectory contained in a sufficiently small neighborhood of q has at most k switching points, and set sw(q) = infinity if arbitrarily small neighborhoods of q contain time-optimal trajectories with infinitely many switching points. Is sw(q) finite for every point q in M?
target_in_paper: Section I.A, Singularities of time-optimal trajectories: for a generic pair (f,g) of smooth vector fields on a 3-dimensional manifold M, whether the local switching-count invariant sw(q) is finite at every point q, i.e. whether sw(q) < ∞ for all q ∈ M. The paper presents this as an open question rather than as a numbered conjecture. ([paperzz.com](https://paperzz.com/doc/7063141/some-open-problems---sissa-people-personal-home-pages))
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the paper’s main object and main question: it uses the 3-dimensional single-input control-affine system q̇ = f(q) + u g(q), |u| ≤ 1; it introduces the same local invariant sw(q) based on switching points in sufficiently small neighborhoods of q; and it asks the exact local finiteness question sw(q) < ∞ for every q ∈ M. That is the precise open problem stated in Section I.A for generic 3-dimensional systems. ([paperzz.com](https://paperzz.com/doc/7063141/some-open-problems---sissa-people-personal-home-pages))

refined_question: Let M be a 3-dimensional smooth manifold, and let f, g be a generic pair of smooth vector fields on M. Consider the fixed-endpoint time-optimal control problem q̇ = f(q) + u g(q), with |u| ≤ 1, where admissible controls are measurable and admissible trajectories are Lipschitz. A switching point of an admissible trajectory is a point where the trajectory is not smooth. For q ∈ M, define sw(q) to be the smallest integer k such that every time-optimal trajectory whose image is contained in some sufficiently small neighborhood of q has at most k switching points, and set sw(q) = ∞ if every neighborhood of q contains a time-optimal trajectory with infinitely many switching points. Is sw(q) < ∞ for every q ∈ M? ([paperzz.com](https://paperzz.com/doc/7063141/some-open-problems---sissa-people-personal-home-pages))
justification: This is the nearest paper-faithful formulation because Section I.A first motivates the generic problem by asking whether optimal trajectories are piecewise smooth, then specializes to the 3-dimensional case by defining sw(q), records the partial results sw(q) = 2 outside a 2-dimensional Whitney stratified subset and sw(q) ≤ 4 outside a 1-dimensional Whitney stratified subset, and then asks whether sw(q) is finite for every q ∈ M. The paper also states separately that finiteness of switching points for each individual time-optimal trajectory would be only a weaker property, so that weaker statement should not replace the sw(q)-question. On the next page, the author adds that the generic 3-dimensional problem is the most interesting among the time-optimality questions listed there. ([paperzz.com](https://paperzz.com/doc/7063141/some-open-problems---sissa-people-personal-home-pages))
